title: How to choose the right mix of stocks and bonds for your risk profile
description: Asset allocation 101: Finding your personal efficient frontier.
content:
The most important decision you make as an investor is not 'Which stock?' but 'How much stock?' This ratio—Stocks vs. Bonds—determines 90% of your portfolio's volatility and returns. Too many stocks, and you might panic sell during a crash. Too many bonds, and inflation might eat your retirement. Finding the 'Goldilocks' allocation requires balancing your financial need for growth with your emotional tolerance for pain. This guide helps you calculate your number.

Key Takeaways

  • The 60/40 Baseline: The classic moderate portfolio. 60% Stocks (Growth) / 40% Bonds (Stability). Historically returned ~8-9% with moderate drawdowns.
  • Time Horizon Rule: If you need the money in 5 years, you need bonds. If you need it in 30 years, you can afford 100% stocks.
  • The 'Sleep' Test: If a 20% drop in your portfolio value ($100k to $80k) would cause you to lose sleep, you have too many stocks.
  • Glide Path: Your mix should change. Start aggressive (90/10) in your 20s, and glide to conservative (50/50) in retirement.

Why It Matters (US Context)

US Bonds (Treasuries) act as a specific hedge. In many global crises, money flees to the US Dollar and Treasuries, driving their value up while stocks fall. This 'negative correlation' is why US investors rely heavily on bonds for protection.

Standard Allocations

Pick the model that fits your gut.

The Aggressive (90/10 or 100/0)

Who: Under 35, or high risk tolerance.

Expectation: High growth, but wild rides. Can drop 50% in a bad year. Must have 20+ year horizon.

The Balanced (60/40)

Who: Ages 45-55, or nervous investors.

Expectation: Captures ~70% of market upside but only ~60% of the downside. The 'Free Lunch' of diversification.

The Conservative (30/70)

Who: Retirees needing income.

Expectation: Preserves capital. Generates dividends/interest. Growth barely beats inflation.

How to Build It

  1. Use Broad ETFs: Don't overcomplicate.
    - Stock Portion: VTI (Total US) + VXUS (Total Intl).
    - Bond Portion: BND (Total Bond).
  2. Automate Rebalancing: If stocks crash, your 60/40 becomes 50/50. You must sell bonds and buy stocks to get back to 60/40. This forces you to 'Buy Low'.
  3. Bond Tent: 5 years before retirement, aggressively shift to bonds to protect your nest egg from a 'Sequence of Returns' disaster.
  4. Consider Cash: For very conservative investors, Short-Term Treasuries (SGOV) or Cash are now a valid substitute for Bonds given current yields.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why do young people need bonds?

They don't need them for returns, they need them for behavior. A 10% bond allocation can prevent a full panic sale by softening the daily volatility.

Are bonds safe?

They are safer than stocks, but they can lose value if interest rates rise rapidly (like 2022). Short-term bonds are safer than long-term bonds.

What is the '110 Rule'?

110 minus Age = Stock %. If you are 30, 110-30 = 80% Stocks. This is a more modern, aggressive version of the old '100 minus Age' rule.
